In addition to its town-and-gown relationship with Rollins College, the oldest private college in Florida, the city has developed significant partnerships among area businesses, schools, cultural organizations, civic groups and neighborhood associations. BAUGhaus (BOG-house) is a play on the owners married last name "Baugus" and the German art school, Bauhaus, whose mission, not unlike ours, was to provide a space for the arts to be brought together. Coincidentally it translates to -- BAUG [Turkish] "garden" and haus [German] "house" -- garden house. ChIJ3yDG2PML3YgRkX90s-gJI_U.about: Bella Cosa was originally known as Lake Pierce Club and was built in 1925. It was visited by famous people from actors and actresses to the President of the United States. In the 40s and 50s it was renamed as The Bonaire and continued to be a location frequented by people looking for a good time and a wonderful place to stay. Until the end of the 60s it continued to be used as a hotel and then passed through a succession of owners, including a Vietnamese family who housed refugees there. In 2016 it was purchased by Rev. Jim Way, the President of Capernaum Ministeries, at which time it was renamed Capernaum Lakeside Lodge. The Ministry carried out extensive renovations of the property restoring its natural beauty, including restoring the oak flooring and stripping back the walls to their original state. The building changed hands again and renamed Bella Cosa Lakeside Lodge & Venue. It has been used as an exclusive-use wedding venue ever since and is now known simply by the name Bella Cosa. ChIJLQUlX1R554gRN78uS-dPM7Q.about: I Once Threw a Party a Room Full of Board Members Refused to Leave That was thirty five years ago, and I have been chasing that feeling ever since. I founded Diamond Receptions in 2007. Somewhere between that party and this business, I also learned something about money that isn't mine, and it changed how I have run every wedding since. Before any of this, I was the marketing and special events director at a local Chamber of Commerce, and I was handed a problem dressed up as an assignment. The chamber needed an annual meeting for its board of directors, the kind of event where business gets done and everyone claps politely and goes home. I was told to build something bigger than that around it. Make it profitable. Get three quarters of the membership in the room, and understand that in the years before me, people showed up, ate dinner, and left the moment the actual board business started. So I built a gala around it and gave it a name: Putting on the Ritz. Red carpet, spotlights, the whole room dressed for it, and gaming tables scattered through the reception so there was always somewhere for a conversation to keep going. Almost the entire membership came. Nobody left early, not even for the board meeting itself. We raised more money that night than the chamber had ever raised at a single event. It all started when the first group met in the upper room of M. E. Wilson's General Merchandise Store on the southeast corner of 8th & Montrose Street in 1886. The people of Clermont and neighboring towns would hold weekly church services with occasional guest pastors, prayer, hymns, and discuss God's word. In January 1891, 26 people became members of the Methodist faith and thus forming the Methodist Episcopal Church in Clermont. In 1968, the Methodist Church and the Evangelical United Brethren Church united to form the United Methodist Church, thus changing our name to the First United Methodist Church of Clermont. In 2023, our congregation voted to disaffiliate from the United Methodist Church. In April, we rebranded and propelled into the future as Living Hope Church, a Wesleyan Community. ChIJw8T8pyuf54gRF5J0cER8zxY.home: A Step Back In Time - Come Explore the Magic Established in 1883 and remodeled by famous architect Grosvenor Atterbury in 1903, Sydonie was once said to be the most significant residential structure in all of Florida. With a total of 42 rooms and over 22 thousand square feet, Sydonie reflects an era of craftsmanship and unique architecture difficult to find in modern homes. It was originally built as the winter retreat for James Laughlin, who was the owner of J&L Steel in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Sydonie was built in the Mediterranean Revival and asian styles, and primarily designed after Alhambra Castle in Spain. Once a 9000-acre preserve, Sydonie's grounds originally included sculptured gardens with rare plants from around the world, citrus groves, a dairy farm, a power plant, and even a bowling alley. Today, the mansion is available as a wedding and event venue, and is currently open for historic tours.
